Note::to_nfkd¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::to_nfkd() const

Compatibility-Decompose Every Cell To Unicode Normalization Form KD¶

to_nfkd() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with each cell converted to NFKD — full compatibility decomposition with no recomposition. It applies the same compatibility folds as to_nfkc (ﬁ → fi, ² → 2, full-width → plain) but leaves accented letters decomposed, as base letter plus combining marks.

Reach for NFKD when you want both the compatibility folding and the marks exposed for a follow-up pass such as strip_accents. Like NFKC it is lossy — do not use it where the compatibility distinctions carry meaning.

to_nfkd is shape-preserving, cell-independent, idempotent, and returns a fresh Note. Requires the Unicode backend.

Example 1: Compatibility Folds Applied, Accents Left Decomposed¶

const std::string in = std::string("\xEF\xAC\x81") + "le " + "\xC2\xB2";  // ﬁ + "le " + ²
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({in, "plain"}).to_nfkd())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["file 2", "plain"]

"ﬁle ²" becomes "file 2" (this input has no accents to leave decomposed).

  • Note::to_nfkc: the composed compatibility form.

  • Note::to_nfd: canonical decomposition without the compatibility folds.
